newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian gov't proposes central bank legislation.
newsitem.headline: Romanian gov't proposes central bank legislation.

text.p: Romania's government on Sunday presented legislation committing the central bank (BNR) to use monetary policy to achieve price stability in line with European Union (EU) requirements.

Teodor Buftea, an adviser to bank governor Mugur Isarescu, said a new law to be presented to parliament this week was meant to align Romanian policy with the stipulations of the 1992 Maastricht agreement.
"The new law sets down stability of the national currency and stability of prices as the main tasks of the central bank," Buftea told a news conference at the end a cabinet meeting.
He said the new BNR status reinforced the central bank's independence from state institutions other than parliament.
The bill also calls for the reduction of the central bank governor's term to five years from the present eight.

The BNR came under pressure from the leftist government of Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu to ease monetary policy by extending fresh farm subsidies ahead of last year's general election which brought the current centrist coalition to power.
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's new government has pledged to maintain tight monetary policy and rein in subsidies as part of a reform programme backed by international lenders.
